authoring: Direct conversational scientific reasoning and Korean authoring; no external LLM API or generated-content script.
scope_convention: reference_section identifies specific retrieved passages, not whole-paper reading. publisher_abstract includes an author's original arXiv abstract. Short quotations are retrieved evidence; support and limitations are authored paraphrases.
comparison: Compared candidate terms across all canonical groups and read the nearest principles and conditions. Canonical count at nearest-card retrieval was 1798. This batch identifies specific pathways within broad physical parents, not eight unrelated fundamental laws. Mechanical key validation is separate from this semantic review.

evidence.read: Unruh 1976 original paper, Section III Particle Detectors, PDF pages 13-16: proper-time frequency definition, uniformly accelerated detector, equation 3.10 and energy source discussion.
evidence.quote: the detector measures frequencies with respect to its own proper time
evidence.support: Uniform acceleration in Minkowski vacuum yields the response of a thermal bath with temperature proportional to proper acceleration. In the inertial account, the excitation and emitted quantum receive energy from the external accelerating field.
evidence.limitation: Theoretical field-detector model. No direct experimental confirmation is claimed. Black-hole collapse, moving boundary photon production and clock time dilation are distinct neighboring mechanisms; arbitrary nonuniform acceleration is not automatically thermal.

evidence.read: Super-Kamiokande 1998 original experiment, PDF page 1 equation 1 and definitions, pages 4-5 L/E analysis and conclusions.
evidence.quote: the mixing angle between the flavor eigenstates and the mass eigenstates
evidence.support: Vacuum flavor-transition probability depends on mass-squared difference, mixing angle and distance/energy. Atmospheric muon-like event deficit and zenith dependence support an oscillation model. The card states the associated coherent mass/flavor basis mechanism rather than asserting every detail is measured in this paper.
evidence.limitation: Paper explicitly could not distinguish muon-to-tau from muon-to-sterile oscillations in that sample. It neither determines all three-flavor parameters nor proves an absolute neutrino mass. Matter-induced resonance is not counted as another card.

evidence.read: Original author manuscript submitted 2001: first-page abstract and introductory molecular mechanism, target/TOF experimental description. PDF's generated 2018 date is not treated as publication date.
evidence.quote: The muon will be quickly captured by an atom, replacing the orbital electron.
evidence.support: Large muon mass contracts the molecular ion, brings isotope nuclei close and screens their repulsion; fusion can leave the muon available for another cycle. Experiment measures resonant molecular formation through fusion events in solid HD.
evidence.limitation: Formation rates, muon decay and alpha sticking limit cycling. No net-energy claim or universal cycle count. This is an approach/catalysis path within the broad fusion parent, not a second mass-defect energy law.

evidence.read: Original Chandran et al. 2010 author abstract, retrieved in full from arXiv; linked publication DOI 10.1088/0004-637X/720/1/503 verified in record. Full article was not read for this card.
evidence.quote: frequencies smaller than the ion cyclotron frequency
evidence.support: At perpendicular wavelengths near gyroradius and above sufficient fluctuation amplitude, ion orbits become chaotic and energy diffuses through interaction with the time-dependent electrostatic potential. The abstract directly contrasts conserved magnetic moment at weak fluctuation with its violation at stronger fluctuation.
evidence.limitation: Phenomenology and test-particle simulations. The reported numerical threshold applies to those random-phase simulations, not all plasmas. Distinct from frequency-matched cyclotron absorption and phase-speed Landau resonance.

evidence.read: Original Fecko 1997 manuscript: Introduction, Section 4 conserved momenta, Section 5.2 disc/internal point-mass example and Section 5.3 N-particle construction.
evidence.quote: which is just vanishing of the total angular momentum of the system
evidence.support: Internal shape coordinates determine compensating body rotation under zero total angular momentum. Section 5.2 explicitly integrates the connection around a closed shape loop and obtains a nonzero orientation change. The broad deformable-body formulation covers the classical falling-cat route.
evidence.limitation: Mechanical theory, not a biological claim about every cat movement. Energy for deformation remains necessary. The result changes orientation and does not provide reactionless center-of-mass translation.
evidence.source_history: Montgomery's original author-listed 1993 paper was located, but its image-only PDF yielded no usable text. Screenshot requests did not expose usable image content in the wrapper and are not claimed as reading. A public-file shell retrieval failed with WinError 10013 and was not escalated. Carl's Hamburg file identified itself as a review, so it was not used as the primary binding. Fecko's original derivation supplies the directly read source.

evidence.read: Original Pomeranchuk article, English JETP 8(2), pages 361-362, PDF starts with the end of an unrelated preceding article. Only the section beginning On the Stability of a Fermi Liquid and ending before Orlov's article is used. Equations 1-12 and surrounding derivation read.
evidence.quote: The variations appearing in Eq. (1) are due to deformations of the Fermi surface
evidence.quote_note: OCR delta-n mathematical symbols are omitted in this short normalized excerpt.
evidence.support: The quadratic energy functional is decomposed into angular harmonics, giving mode-specific positivity conditions for Fermi-surface stability. The paper separately notes the spin l=0 criterion for absence of ferromagnetism; this card selects anisotropic shape channels to avoid duplicating the Stoner card.
evidence.limitation: A negative deformation cost establishes instability, not a universal final nematic structure or transition temperature. Fermi-surface topology crossing and stable zero-sound propagation are different nearby cards.

evidence.read: Destrade 2001 original paper on author's university site, Introduction, Section III equations 6-15 for coupled displacement/traction and vanishing boundary values, Section IV equations 23-27 and isotropic limit.
evidence.quote: The surface x2 = 0 is assumed to be free of tractions
evidence.quote_note: Only PDF OCR equation spacing is normalized.
evidence.support: The joint traction-free boundary and depth-decay conditions select a coupled elastic surface mode. The derived subsonic secular equation has a positive solution and recovers the isotropic incompressible Rayleigh result.
evidence.limitation: The cited derivation is for an incompressible orthotropic half-space. The card does not claim a material-independent speed or apply this equation to thin plates. Love/Lamb/Stoneley modes are not added as shape variants.
evidence.source_history: Rayleigh 1885 publisher metadata was verified, but its body was not accessible. A Zenodo reproduction failed retrieval. The fully retrieved modern original derivation is the binding source, not the inaccessible historical paper.

evidence.read: Cho 2011 original manuscript, Introduction equations 1-2, Numerical Method dispersion relation, Section 2 circular polarization equations 4-6. The automatically generated 2018 PDF date is not publication date.
evidence.quote: fast electron flows carry all the current
evidence.support: At sufficiently small ion scales, stationary ions and electron-carried current give a Hall induction equation. Its linear magnetic components form a dispersive propagating whistler mode, distinct from bulk-fluid-inertia Alfven dynamics and electrostatic charge-separation Langmuir dynamics.
evidence.limitation: This selected electron-fluid limit neglects electron inertia; it is not asserted at all frequencies and wavelengths. Inverse cascade and polarization variants are not additional cards.

supplement.support: Describes magnetic energy exchanging between orthogonal magnetic field components. Its PDF retrieval failed, so the card now binds the directly read Cho derivation.
